title: DWV Fittings vs. Pressure Fittings: Crucial Differences
description: Drain, Waste, and Vent (DWV) fittings are engineered specifically for gravity-fed drainage systems, featuring smooth internal radii and shallow sockets to encourage unrestricted flow and prevent buildup. In contrast, pressure fittings have deeper hubs and sharp directional turns built to withstand internal hydraulic pressure, which creates turbulence and severe clog points if used in drainage. Mixing up these fitting types compromises system efficiency and violates plumbing codes. Professional installers must inspect fitting markings, sweep radius, and hub depth to ensure every component matches its intended application within the drainage network.

DWV Fittings vs. Pressure Fittings: Crucial Differences

Drain, Waste, and Vent (DWV) fittings are engineered specifically for gravity-fed drainage systems, featuring smooth internal radii and shallow sockets to encourage unrestricted flow and prevent buildup. In contrast, pressure fittings have deeper hubs and sharp directional turns built to withstand internal hydraulic pressure, which creates turbulence and severe clog points if used in drainage. Mixing up these fitting types compromises system efficiency and violates plumbing codes. Professional installers must inspect fitting markings, sweep radius, and hub depth to ensure every component matches its intended application within the drainage network.
